- Rule → aim **lateral and up** → away from the vertebral artery in front and the root

| Screw | Entry | Direction | Danger |

- Rule → cervical pedicles are safe **only at C2 and C7**

5B.09.t: Anterior Lumbar Approaches — ALIF, Transperitoneal & LLIF
5B.09.b:
### Retroperitoneal ALIF
- ALIF (anterior lumbar interbody fusion) → **L5–S1 between the iliac vessels; L4–5 above the bifurcation**
  [[FIG: Fig 5B.80, 5B.81, 5B.82, 5B.83, 5B.84, 5B.85, 5B.86 · 5B.09
- Position → supine, slight lordosis · Incision → Pfannenstiel for L5–S1, or paramedian
- Interval → medial to and under the rectus (segmental T7–T12) → behind the peritoneum

1) Rectus lifted → below the **arcuate line** → peritoneum swept medially
2) Psoas lateral, ureter with peritoneum
3) Ligate middle sacral (L5–S1) or **iliolumbar vein** (L4–5)

### Dangers
- **Left common iliac vein** lies flat over L5–S1 → the most fragile structure
  [[FIG: Fig 5B.87, 5B.88, 5B.89, 5B.90, 5B.91 · 5B.09

- At risk → left common iliac vein, IVC · iliolumbar vein (ligate **before** retracting) · **superior hypogastric plexus** (**no cautery**) · ureter · sympathetic chain

- Plexus injury → **retrograde ejaculation** (not impotence), up to 20%

PITFALL — level of the aortic bifurcation
- Hopp → on the anterior surface of **L4**; Kim → at the **L4–5 disc**
- Say → "L4 to L4–5; L5–S1 lies in the V below it → check the MRI" (AO)

MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "ALIF at L5–S1"
- Supine; rectus lifted, enter below the arcuate line; peritoneum + ureter medial
- **Between the iliac vessels**; ligate middle sacral vessels (L4–5 → iliolumbar vein)
- No cautery over the promontory → plexus → retrograde ejaculation · most fragile → left common iliac vein
